clinician.final_diagnosis: ALK+ histiocytosis with pathological features of juvenile xanthogranulomatosis (JXG)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 2-month-old full-term male infant presented with worsening tachypnoea and a rapidly enlarging, smooth-topped, infiltrative, bronze-yellow nodule with telangiectasias on the mid-sternum. CT imaging revealed multiple pulmonary nodules and extradural masses compressing L4-L5 neural foramina. Immunohistochemical staining of skin and pulmonary lesion biopsies demonstrated a highly proliferative histiocytosis positive for ALK, CD33, factor XIIIa, weak CD68, and negative for lineage markers such as CD1a and Langerin, consistent with juvenile xanthogranulomatosis features. Molecular genetic testing identified a KIF5B-ALK fusion rearrangement, confirming ALK+ histiocytosis. Whole body MRI and PET/CT showed FDG-avid lesions in the lungs, spinal cord compressive sites, a metabolic right meningeal/parietal brain tumor, and mediastinal/abdominal lymphadenopathy. These combined clinical, imaging, pathological, and molecular findings support the diagnosis of ALK+ histiocytosis with JXG features.
